paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of Shiloh. Hannah took her ache straight to the LORD. Year after year she was taunted until she wept and would not eat, and then she stood up and prayed "out of the depth of my anguish and grief" (1 Samuel 1:16). She didn't have to dress it up first. She poured out her soul before the LORD (1 Samuel 1:15), and that's an invitation for every baker holding a heavy batch right now.

Look at what happens next, because it matters. Eli said, "Go in peace," and Hannah began to eat, and her face was no longer downcast (1 Samuel 1:17-18). Her baby wasn't even born yet! I think she walked out lighter because she'd handed the weight to Someone who could carry it. Then the LORD remembered her, and when her son came she kept her vow and dedicated him to the LORD (1 Samuel 1:19, 28). I'm not saying every prayer gets answered the way hers did. I'm saying the LORD hears every one, and a promise made to Him in the dark is still worth keeping in the light.

And her song in chapter 2 tells us who she was talking to. "There is no one holy like the LORD," and "There is no Rock like our God" (1 Samuel 2:2). He raises the poor from the dust, lifts the needy from the ash heap, and "by his own strength shall no man prevail" (1 Samuel 2:8-9). So here's your big idea, friend: you don't have to be strong enough, because He is the strong one. Bring Him the whole thing, tears and all. I know what it is to lie under the dust, and I promise you, the LORD is good at lifting! This story isn't over, so keep your apron on.
